customer: I've been trying to sort out selling my dad's old car for him while juggling a newborn, and nobody can give me a straight answer on what I actually need. He's in Eastvale and can't come in himself, so can I just bring his car in? I don't have time for multiple trips with a baby in the back of my wagon.
agent: I'm sorry this has been confusing. Congratulations on the new baby, too. According to our article "Selling a family member's car for them," you can sell your dad's car for him if he gives you a power of attorney. He'll need to sign form NW-POA-1 in front of a notary, and then you can bring that form along with your own photo ID and the car's documents, which are listed in our What to bring article. Having all of that together should let you handle it in one visit.
